title: Delele (Zimbabwean slippery okra relish)
steps: Wash the okra, cut off the stalk ends and chop the pods very finely, almost to a paste, because the stickiness is what the dish is known for.
Bring the water to a boil in a medium pot and stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
Add the chopped okra and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it turns bright green, soft and slippery.
While the okra cooks, heat the oil in a separate pan and fry the onion for about 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the tomatoes to the onion and cook for another 5 minutes until they break down into a thick sauce.
Tip the tomato and onion mixture into the okra, add the peanut butter if using, and stir well.
Simmer for 5 more minutes, season with salt and add a splash of water if it becomes too thick.
Serve hot as a relish beside sadza or any thick maize porridge, scooping it up with small balls of porridge.

title: Kapenta with tomato and onion (Zimbabwean fried dried sardines)

ingredients.name: dried kapenta (small dried freshwater sardines; dried anchovies are a substitute)

steps: Rinse the dried kapenta briefly in cold water, then soak for 10 minutes so the fish soften slightly, and drain well.
Pat the fish dry with a clean cloth so they fry rather than steam.
Heat half of the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the fish for 3 to 4 minutes until lightly crisp, then lift them out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and fry the onions for 5 minutes until soft and just starting to brown, adding the garlic and chilli for the last minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for about 8 minutes until they collapse into a thick sauce.
Return the kapenta to the pan, sprinkle over the ground peanuts and stir gently so the fish are coated.
Add a splash of water and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, tasting before adding salt because the fish are already salty.
Serve hot with sadza and a side of cooked greens.
